subject: A Few Questions from a Newbie about Getting Started with devtools

messages.author: d48c25039d976859
messages.subject: A Few Questions from a Newbie about Getting Started with devtools
parts: I consider myself a novice to intermediate R programmer and have a few good ideas for libraries that I would move forward with. I am a newbie in terms of developing libraries and I have no experience building R libraries but would like to get that understanding. I have pretty much no experience with GitHub but I do have an account. I have devtools installed. My first question is, how to initialize a new project and can devtools automatically create a GitHub repository under my user name and install the correct directory structure there. I am guessing that this is the case because of the install_github() command in devtools although I'm not sure. Can somebody provide with some clear insight how to "sync my application from my computer with my GitHub repository", also can somebody please explain the idea of pull request?

messages.author: 8ffd6137fd43c6df
messages.subject: Re: A Few Questions from a Newbie about Getting Started with devtools
parts: Congratulations on taking the next step, and good look with your package ideas.  If you're going to learn package development, I recommend reading Hadley's  R Packages book.  Not only will it answer most developer's existing and upcoming questions, it will reframe the situation and make their approach more coherent/consistent.  But here are pointers for your specific questions.  They're great questions for someone at this stage, and fortunately a lot of good stuff exists to answer them.
how to initialize a new project and can devtools automatically create a GitHub repository under my user name and install the correct directory structure there.
The best place to start is probably the package chapter and the GitHub chapter.
I am guessing that this is the case because of the install_github() command in devtools although I'm not sure.
This function is actually for installing other people's packages that are hosted on GitHub.  Its primary purpose is not for developing your own package.
Can somebody provide with some clear insight how to "sync my application from my computer with my GitHub repository", also can somebody please explain the idea of pull request?

Within the world of R packages, see the "Making a pull request" section, toward the end of the GitHub chapter.  One of the successful strategies of RStudio developers is that they build on existing frameworks and approaches; one advantage is that you can exploit that much larger non-R world's knowledge.  For example, in the GitHub Guides, I recommend starting with Getting your project on GitHub and Understanding the GitHub Flow.
